title: Choose a Homework Time Together | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: Your nine-year-old reaches the homework table already tired, and the first question turns into a daily argument. There is no single perfect homework time; insisting on one schedule without noticing the child's energy can add conflict. Pause and discuss the routine when neither of you is in the middle of the struggle. Offer a workable plan: snack and a short movement break, then homework at the same quiet table; agree on the start cue together. A regular place and predictable time reduce repeated decisions, while ongoing schoolwork concerns belong in a conversation with the teacher.

claim_limits: Suggested wording is an example, not a guaranteed result.
Adapt expectations to the individual child and safety context.
